transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-05-28
Time: 08:43 PDT
Duration: ~54 mins
Attendees: Jordan (Redwood AE), Maya (Redwood SE), Carlos (Redwood CSM), Linda (Head of MLOps, Northbridge), Rajesh (VP Eng), Emily (SecOps), Tom (SRE)

Auto-summary (auto):
- Kickoff orientation for implementation runway, discuss SLA expectations, networking/VPC constraints, and encryption/KMS requirements.
- Align on pilot scope, success criteria, timeline and next steps including runbook and Terraform artifacts.

Topics (auto):
- Deployment mode: Dedicated vs Private (VPC)
- Security: KMS/HSM, SOC2 mentions, SSO/SAML, audit logs
- Performance: latency targets, batching, KV cache
- Ops runbook and rollback

Transcript:
[00:00] Jordan Lee: Hey everyone thanks for joining on time, um we'll kick off — I'm Jordan, AE, with Maya our SE and Carlos CSM, uh this is the initial ops orientation walk through for the Northbridge pilot.
[00:22] Linda Park: Hi all, thanks. Quick note we're running a tight timeline, we'd like a pilot verified in the next 3 weeks if possible.
[00:35] Maya Patel: Got it. We'll try to be pragmatic. Today we'll go over deployment options, expected latencies, the SLA matrix and what we need from you to scope the smoke test.
[00:49] Rajesh Iyer: The big constraints: everything has to be within our VPC, and we need customer-managed keys, plus audit logs forwarded to our SIEM. Also, any PII must never leave region eu-west-1.
[01:10] Emily Chen: And from security side we need SAML SSO + RBAC, SOC2 and FedRAMP-ish controls are a hard ask for later, for now SOC2 reports and pen test results would be great.
[01:28] Maya Patel: Understood. On Private deployments we offer a private control plane option so we can keep traffic inside your VPC. For KMS we integrate with major providers, we also support HSM via customer KMS for key wrapping. There are a few config knobs around token retention and audit log retention.
[01:50] Tom Rivers: Couple of specifics: we run NAT across multiple AZs, can Redwood support multi-AZ peering? Also what's the ip range requirement, we prefer a minimal allowlist.
[02:06] Jordan Lee: Yes, multi-AZ is supported. We'll ask for a small set of egress IPs for the link, we can also do peering or transit gateway. We'll send a sample network diagram and the terraform example.
[02:27] Linda Park: Great. On success criteria: key metrics for us are 95th percentile latency under 350ms for standard prompt gen at 512 tokens and throughput of ~60 reqs/min sustained, with less than 0.1% error rate. Are those realistic?
[02:50] Maya Patel: 350ms at 512 tokens is aggressive on our standard hosted stack but doable on Dedicated with small batching and nvlink-backed instances; we'll propose a quantized variant and a warm KV cache for the pilot to get close. We should run a perf benchmark-off with your sample prompts.
[03:12] Rajesh Iyer: What's the plan for model rollouts and can we pin model versions? We need deterministic behavior during the pilot.
[03:23] Jordan Lee: Absolutely, you can pin model versions in the deployment config and we have canary rollouts and immediate fallback policies in case of regressions.
[03:34] Emily Chen: Audit logs — we need immutable logs for two years, is that supported? Also, can logs be forwarded to Splunk?
[03:46] Maya Patel: We can stream audit logs to your SIEM, Splunk is supported via HTTP forwarder or S3 then ingestion. Retention policies are configurable; two years is part of our enterprise add-on.
[04:02] Tom Rivers: On networking latency — curious about the prefix caching and KV cache behavior across region boundaries, if the KV cache is in Redwood-managed infra does it cross the VPC?
[04:17] Maya Patel: For private deployments KV cache lives in your VPC; for hosted it's in Redwood infra but we do prefix caching and edge routing to minimize hops. For pilot we'll recommend keeping KV in your VPC to avoid cross region reads.
[04:33] Jordan Lee: Quick note, we've seen customers reduce token cost by 20-40% with prefix caching and aggressive batching on non-latency critical routes.
[04:46] Linda Park: Good, cost is important, but SLA is top priority. How do you handle graceful degradation? If Dedicated nodes are saturated what happens?
[04:59] Maya Patel: We have smart routing policies: traffic can failover to a compatible cheaper model variant or degrade to lower quality at the same latency bracket. For critical routes you can set automatic fallback to a cold standby model in another region.
[05:15] Rajesh Iyer: Ok, since we run regulated workloads we want an explicit data residency guarantee and a runbook for failover.
[05:25] Carlos Nuñez: We'll deliver a runbook draft after this call; it includes failover steps, rollback, and escalation paths, and we'll iterate with your SRE.
[05:36] Linda Park: Perfect. Let's talk timeline — Rajesh said 3 weeks, is that realistic for pilot?
[05:42] Maya Patel: For a smoke pilot with limited traffic and pinned model I'd say 2-4 weeks depending on how fast you provide the network artifacts and KMS decisions.
[05:51] Tom Rivers: We'll need to run a security review internally too, that might add 1 week.
[05:58] Emily Chen: I'll own the security review and get you a list of questions.
[06:03] Jordan Lee: Great — action items we'll capture.
[06:09]
[10:12] Linda Park: Quick question about telemetry — what level of per-token cost visibility do we get in the console? We want token-level breakdown by route and model.
[10:24] Maya Patel: The Console exposes token-level charts per model/route and we also can export CSVs with token counts, latencies, and cost allocation. For pilots we'll share a short dashboard template.
[10:40] Rajesh Iyer: Any special steps for canarying model updates? We have strict change control.
[10:47] Maya Patel: We support canary percentages, A/B rollout, and automatic regression alerts tied to prompt sets. You can lock rollouts behind approvals in the console — or we can integrate with your CI to gate rollouts.
[11:05]
[15:30] Emily Chen: On KMS: do you support AWS KMS with BYOK? We need keys we control.
[15:37] Maya Patel: Yes BYOK supported. You can configure the key to live in your account; Redwood will request wrapped keys for runtime operations. For on-prem/HSM we'll need additional integration steps.
[15:49] Emily Chen: Also need evidence for SOC2 and any pen test summaries.
[15:54] Jordan Lee: We will share SOC2 Type II reports and our pen test summary redacted for any customer-sensitive details.
[16:02]
[19:10] Tom Rivers: For the pilot, what's the typical sequence? Do you ask us to feed sample workloads, then you run benchmarking and then a staged rollout?
[19:20] Maya Patel: Typical: 1) collect sample prompts, sequence length distribution, and concurrency profile; 2) run perf bench on Dedicated or Private preview; 3) tune KV cache and batching; 4) run smoke test inside your VPC; 5) evaluate against success criteria then toggle to steady-state. We'll provide a checklist.
[19:39] Linda Park: We'll send sample prompts and a CSV of historical latencies.
[19:44] Rajesh Iyer: Who do we loop in for billing? Also, are there reserved commit options?
[19:51] Jordan Lee: I'll introduce finance contact once the pilot converges. We do have reserved capacity pricing for Dedicated; I'll include both on-demand and reserved options in the pricing spreadsheet.
[19:59]
[24:00] Maya Patel: Small note on observability: our trace hooks can be added to your app to capture token-level traces; we can also forward traces to Jaeger or Honeycomb.
[24:12] Tom Rivers: We prefer Honeycomb. Any sample instrumentation snippets?
[24:18] Maya Patel: Yes, we'll share sample SDK hooks and a short troubleshooting runbook.
[24:26]
[29:05] Linda Park: On compliance docs — would you be able to provide a list of sub processors and any data flow diagrams?
[29:13] Carlos Nuñez: Yes we'll share an asset pack: SOC2 report, sub-processor list, data flow, and controls matrix. We'll redact customer-specific info.
[29:22] Emily Chen: Good. Also curious about retention of ephemeral prompt data — is that configurable?
[29:28] Maya Patel: Yes retention windows are configurable per route; for pilot we'll set strict retention.
[29:35]
[34:50] Rajesh Iyer: For performance tuning, you mentioned quantized model variant. Are there expected quality regressions we should measure?
[35:00] Maya Patel: There can be small quality delta; we'll propose an eval harness with a small prompt set to measure ROUGE/BLEU-ish metrics and manual review for subjective quality. We can tie regression alerts to that harness.
[35:12] Linda Park: Who owns the evaluator runs? We'll probably do internal QA but Redwood can provide baseline.
[35:18] Maya Patel: We'll run a baseline and hand you the harness, then you can run it in your CI for each rollout.
[35:25]
[40:01] Jordan Lee: Quick recap of outstanding asks: 1) Network diagram & allowlist 2) KMS choice 3) sample prompts and latency CSV 4) sign-off on pilot dates.
[40:12] Linda Park: We'll aim to send network diagram and KMS decision by 06/03. Sample prompts will go out by end of week.
[40:20] Carlos Nuñez: We'll send runbook draft + TF example by 06/02 and a Dedicated pricing spreadsheet.
[40:28] Tom Rivers: I'll compile the allowlist and peering constraints and share before 06/03.
[40:34]
[45:22] Emily Chen: One more question, how do you handle eDiscovery and log export for legal hold?
[45:31] Jordan Lee: We can export immutable snapshots of audit logs for eDiscovery; details depend on your retention policies but it's supported as part of the enterprise package.
[45:42]
[50:00] Linda Park: Sounds good. Any blockers from Redwood side?
[50:04] Maya Patel: Nope, we just need the artifacts mentioned. We'll prepare the pilot checklist and a perf runbook.
[50:11] Jordan Lee: I'll follow up with a calendar invite for the pilot kickoff and include the contact list.
[50:18] Carlos Nuñez: Action items recapped and I'll document them in the ticket.
[50:25]
[53:00] Linda Park: Thanks everyone, appreciate the clarity.
[53:05] Jordan Lee: Thanks all, we'll be in touch and expect the runbook and pricing in the next 48 hours.

Shared artifacts referenced:
